# Code and accessibility tree

> Status: AI-drafted, not human-reviewed

Group id: `code-and-tree`. Read the markup, the rendered DOM and the browser's accessibility tree to decide questions about names, roles, states, relationships, language and structure. Everything here can be collected by a script without judgement; most judgements are comparisons between what the page shows and what the tree exposes.

## Setup

- Chromium, viewport 1280 x 800, zoom 100%, light colour scheme, JavaScript on, fresh profile.
- Tools: browser DevTools (Elements, Accessibility panel) or a script using the Chrome DevTools Protocol (`Accessibility.getFullAXTree`); the Nu HTML Checker (open source) for parsing errors.
- A person: DevTools plus an HTML validator. An AI: a model that can read long HTML and a JSON accessibility tree; for 1.1.1 and 1.3.1 also a vision model that sees the screenshot.
- Do not use a screen reader in this pass; the tree is the proxy. Real announcement is checked in the screen-reader pass.

## Collect

Collect all of this before judging. Each item names the data type (`needs` key in the data file). A script or a cheap model can do it without judgement; store each artifact with a file name that the report can cite.

1. **dom** — Save the page source as served (before scripts) and the serialised rendered DOM after load plus 2 seconds (`document.documentElement.outerHTML`).
2. **accessibility-tree** — Save the full accessibility tree as JSON. For every node keep: role, accessible name, accessible description, value, states and properties (expanded, checked, selected, disabled, required, invalid, live), and the CSS selector of its DOM node.
3. **dom** — Inventory of non-text content: every `img`, `svg`, `canvas`, `object`, `embed`, `area`, `input[type=image]`, `[role=img]`, `video`, `audio` and every element with a CSS `background-image` that is not a gradient. Per item: selector, source URL, `alt` attribute (present or absent, value), computed accessible name, rendered width and height, whether inside a link or button.
4. **screenshot** — Full-page screenshot at 1280 px, plus a cropped screenshot of every item in the inventory above.
5. **dom** — Inventory of interactive elements (`a[href]`, `button`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `summary`, `[role]`, `[tabindex]`, elements with click handlers): selector, role, accessible name, visible text (`innerText`), `autocomplete` value, input `type`, associated label element(s).
6. **dom** — Structure inventory: headings (level, text), landmarks (role, name), lists, tables (caption, `th`, `scope`, `headers`, `id` references), fieldsets and legends, `lang` of `html` and of every element that has one, `title`, `meta` refresh and viewport, all `id` values that occur more than once.
7. **dom** — Skip mechanism: the first 5 focusable elements in DOM order; for each `a[href^="#"]` among them whether the target id exists, and whether the target is focusable or sits in a landmark.
8. **dom** — Parsing check: run the Nu HTML Checker on the source as served and store the messages (type, message, line).
9. **interaction** — For every custom widget (role tab, menu, combobox, dialog, switch, or any element with `aria-expanded` or `aria-pressed`): record the accessibility-tree node, activate it once with the mouse and once with Enter or Space, record the node again, and store the difference in states and values.

## Judge

Compare three views of each item: what it looks like (screenshot), what the markup says, and what the tree exposes. Judge on the tree.

### 1.1.1 Non-text Content (A)

- **Fails when:** An informative image has no text alternative (F65) or one that is a filename or placeholder (F30); a decorative image is not marked as decorative, or has alt text such as "spacer" (F39, F38); information is conveyed only by a CSS background image (F3); the alternative does not say what the image conveys in context; the alternative is not updated when the image changes (F20).
- **Passes when:** Each informative image has a name that gives its purpose or content in context; decorative images have `alt=""` or are hidden from the tree; an image inside a link or button is named by the link or button; complex images have a short name plus a long description nearby.
- **Common false positives:** axe or HTMLCS reports an image with `alt=""` that is decorative or whose meaning is given by adjacent text; icons inside a button that already has a visible text name; logos whose alt is the organisation name.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** A chart or diagram whose full equivalence you cannot verify; an image whose purpose depends on context you do not have; a CAPTCHA (check the alternative modes exist, otherwise `cantTell`).
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-content.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F3, F13, F20, F30, F38, F39, F65, F67, F71, F72 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (A)

- **Fails when:** Visual structure is not in the markup: text that looks like a heading, list or table is not marked up as one (F2, F43, F33, F34, F48); table headers are missing or wrongly associated (F91, F90); a layout table carries data-table semantics (F46); required state or grouping is shown visually only; a script-made control imitates a link (F42).
- **Passes when:** What the screenshot shows as headings, lists, tables, groups, emphasis and required fields is exposed with matching roles and relationships in the tree.
- **Common false positives:** Bold text that is only emphasis; a `div` list exposed through `role=list`; axe `p-as-heading` on a short styled paragraph; layout tables with presentational role.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** Visual structure in an image or canvas; complex layouts where you cannot tell what the intended relationship is.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/info-and-relationships.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F2, F33, F34, F42, F43, F46, F48, F90, F91, F92, F111 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (AA)

- **Fails when:** A field that collects the user's own data (name, address, e-mail, telephone, card number, birth date, username, password) has no `autocomplete` token or a wrong one (F107).
- **Passes when:** A valid token from the HTML autofill list matches the field's purpose; fields not about the user (search, another person's address) need none.
- **Common false positives:** axe `autocomplete-valid` accepts a token that is valid but wrong for the field; `autocomplete="off"` on fields that do not collect user data.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** The field's purpose is ambiguous from label and context.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/identify-input-purpose.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F107 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 1.3.6 Identify Purpose (AAA)

- **Fails when:** Landmarks, regions, controls or icons whose purpose cannot be determined programmatically: no `main`/`nav`/`header`/`footer`, icon buttons without a name that says their purpose.
- **Passes when:** Regions use landmark elements or roles; icon controls expose their purpose by name or vocabulary.
- **Common false positives:** axe `region` and `landmark-one-main` are best-practice rules, not WCAG-tagged; do not report their output as a failure on its own.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** Which icons or components need a defined purpose is interpretive; give `cantTell` unless the failure is a missing landmark structure.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/identify-purpose.html>

### 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks (A)

- **Fails when:** Repeated blocks (navigation, header) before the main content and no skip link, no landmarks, no headings that let the user bypass them; a skip link whose target does not exist (HTMLCS G123 sniff) or does not move focus.
- **Passes when:** The first focusable element is a working skip link, or `main`/landmark regions and a heading structure exist (both are accepted techniques).
- **Common false positives:** A one-block page has nothing to bypass: `inapplicable`; axe `bypass` passes on headings alone, which is acceptable.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** The skip link appears only under a condition you did not reach.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/bypass-blocks.html>

### 2.4.2 Page Titled (A)

- **Fails when:** The `title` is missing or empty (F25), the same for all pages, a filename or "Untitled", or does not describe topic or purpose.
- **Passes when:** A `title` that identifies this page, distinct from other pages in the set.
- **Common false positives:** HTMLCS always emits a notice about title meaning; only the content of the title decides.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** The title depends on app state after interaction you did not perform.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/page-titled.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F25 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 2.4.9 Link Purpose (Link Only) (AAA)

- **Fails when:** A link's own text is non-specific ("click here", "more", a bare URL) with no mechanism to change it (F84), or an image-only link has no name (F89); identical names point to different destinations.
- **Passes when:** The accessible name alone says what the link is for.
- **Common false positives:** Two links with the same name and the same destination; visually hidden text that completes the name counts as part of the name.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** Names that are specific only to domain experts.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/link-purpose-link-only.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F84, F89 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 2.4.10 Section Headings (AAA)

- **Fails when:** Long content with distinct sections and no headings to organise them.
- **Passes when:** Sections have headings (or an equivalent structure, such as a labelled region).
- **Common false positives:** Short pages; headings used only for interface chrome.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** It is unclear whether a block is a separate section.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/section-headings.html>

### 2.5.3 Label in Name (A)

- **Fails when:** A control with visible text has an accessible name that does not contain that text (F96), for example visible "Search" and `aria-label="Find"`; visible text is split or reordered in the name.
- **Passes when:** The name contains the visible label text, ideally at its start; compare case-insensitively with whitespace normalised.
- **Common false positives:** Visible labels that are symbols or images (non-text); text that is only decoration; punctuation or digits; axe `label-content-name-mismatch` is experimental.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** The visible label is an image of text and you cannot read it reliably.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/label-in-name.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F96, F111 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 3.1.1 Language of Page (A)

- **Fails when:** `lang` is missing (`html`), invalid, or does not match the main language of the page.
- **Passes when:** A valid BCP 47 code that matches the dominant language.
- **Common false positives:** `xml:lang` on HTML pages; an intentionally multilingual page where the main language is clear.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** A page with no dominant language.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/language-of-page.html>

### 3.1.2 Language of Parts (AA)

- **Fails when:** A passage or phrase in another language than the page, without a `lang` attribute, or with a wrong one.
- **Passes when:** Passages are marked; proper names, technical terms and words that have entered the surrounding language need no marking.
- **Common false positives:** Loan words, brand names, names of people and places, code samples.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** Very short phrases whose language is ambiguous.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/language-of-parts.html>

### 3.2.5 Change on Request (AAA)

- **Fails when:** Context changes without being requested by the user: automatic redirect (F40, F41), a new window opened on page load (F52), or on activation without advance notice.
- **Passes when:** Changes happen only on user request, or the user is warned before, or can turn the behaviour off.
- **Common false positives:** A link with `target="_blank"` and a warning in its name; a change of content that is not a change of context.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** It is unclear whether a pop-up was caused by a user action.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/change-on-request.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F60, F61, F9, F22, F52, F40, F41 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (A)

- **Fails when:** A control has no label or instruction that can be perceived and programmatically associated; a placeholder is the only label; a required field or a needed format is not indicated, or only by colour (F82); instructions are not associated with the field.
- **Passes when:** Every input has a visible label tied to it, and needed instructions (format, required) are present before the input.
- **Common false positives:** Hidden fields; a search field whose button text names it; a label provided by `aria-labelledby` (valid).
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** Whether the provided instruction is enough for this audience.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F82 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 4.1.1 Parsing (A)

- **Fails when:** Duplicate `id` values, duplicated attributes, elements not properly nested or not closed in a way that changes the parsed DOM. Note: removed from WCAG 2.2 (always satisfied); under 2.0 and 2.1 conformance a failure still counts.
- **Passes when:** The validator reports no parsing errors of these kinds.
- **Common false positives:** Validator messages about unknown ARIA, obsolete elements, or attributes are not parsing errors in the WCAG sense; duplicate ids inside separate shadow roots are not duplicates.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** The source is invalid but the DOM that the browser builds is fine for assistive technology: report `cantTell` with low confidence and state the WCAG version.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/parsing.html>

### 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A)

- **Fails when:** A control with no accessible name (F68); a script-made control without role (F59); states or values not exposed or not updated when they change (F20); focusable elements hidden from the tree with `aria-hidden`; the accessible name differs from the visible label.
- **Passes when:** Name, role, state and value are exposed in the tree and change when the control is operated.
- **Common false positives:** Names provided by `title`; axe `aria-hidden-focus` on off-screen focusable content that is not reachable.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** Custom widgets whose expected pattern is unclear; actual announcements (see the screen-reader pass).
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/name-role-value.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F59, F15, F20, F42, F68, F79, F86, F89, F111 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded) (A)

Also checked in `time-media`. Here only record whether `audio`/`video` elements exist and whether a transcript link or text alternative is programmatically associated (adjacent link, `aria-describedby`, `figcaption`). Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-only-and-video-only-prerecorded.html>

### 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence (A)

Also checked in `screen-reader`. Here only supply DOM order and the CSS properties that reorder content (`order`, `flex-direction: *-reverse`, `grid-area`, absolute positioning, floats). Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/meaningful-sequence.html>

### 1.4.1 Use of Color (A)

Also checked in `visual`. Here supply the computed `text-decoration` and colour of links inside text blocks; a link with no underline and only a colour difference is a candidate. Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html>

### 2.1.1 Keyboard (A)

Also checked in `keyboard`. Here list elements that have mouse handlers but are not natively focusable and have no `tabindex`; these are candidates for the keyboard pass. Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/keyboard.html>

### 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) (A)

Also checked in `screen-reader` ([recipe](./screen-reader.md)). In this pass, supply the collected data to that judgement; give an outcome here only for a clear failure. Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/link-purpose-in-context.html>

### 2.4.6 Headings and Labels (AA)

Also checked in `language-cognition`. Here supply the headings and labels as the tree exposes them. Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/headings-and-labels.html>

### 3.2.4 Consistent Identification (AA)

Also checked in `visual`. Here supply accessible names of same-function components for cross-page comparison. Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-identification.html>

### 4.1.3 Status Messages (AA)

Also checked in `screen-reader`. Here list live regions (`role=status|alert|log`, `aria-live`) already present in the DOM before any interaction. Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html>

## Already covered by tools

Our retest showed that axe and HTML_CodeSniffer catch missing and empty markup well (labels, alt, link names, lang) but not whether a text is appropriate, whether visual structure is mirrored in markup, or whether state changes reach the tree.

- **1.1.1** (partial) axe: image-alt, input-image-alt, area-alt, object-alt, role-img-alt, svg-img-alt; HTML_CodeSniffer: 1_1_1.H37, 1_1_1.H36, 1_1_1.H30.2, 1_1_1.H67.1, 1_1_1.G94.Image. Retest (15 failing cases): axe 4 flagged, 11 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 4 flagged, 1 asked for review, 5 notice, 5 missed. Rules detect missing or empty alternatives; whether the text is equivalent, or the image decorative, is only flagged as a notice.
- **1.3.1** (partial) axe: label, td-has-header, th-has-data-cells, td-headers-attr, list, listitem, definition-list, dlitem, aria-required-children, aria-required-parent, p-as-heading; HTML_CodeSniffer: 1_3_1.F68, 1_3_1.F92,ARIA4, 1_3_1.H42, 1_3_1.H48, 1_3_1.H63.1, 1_3_1.H71.SameName, 1_3_1_AAA.G141. Retest (13 failing cases): axe 7 flagged, 6 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 5 flagged, 3 notice, 5 missed. Rules catch broken or missing markup patterns; structure that is visual only (bold text as headings, text lists, layout tables) is mostly a notice or missed.
- **1.3.5** (partial) axe: autocomplete-valid; HTML_CodeSniffer: 1_3_5.H98. Retest (2 failing cases): axe 1 flagged, 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 asked for review, 1 notice. axe validates autocomplete values that are present; neither tool can know which fields collect data about the user, so missing autocomplete is at best a notice.
- **1.3.6** (partial) axe: region, landmark-one-main; HTML_CodeSniffer: 1_3_6.ARIA11. Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 flagged; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. Landmark rules (axe best-practice, not WCAG-tagged) catch missing regions; purpose of icons and components is not checked.
- **2.4.1** (partial) axe: bypass; HTML_CodeSniffer: 2_4_1.H64.1, 2_4_1.G1,G123,G124.NoSuchID. No test case in the 2026 retest. axe checks for a skip link, heading or landmark; HTML_CodeSniffer checks skip-link targets and frame titles. Whether the mechanism works is not tested.
- **2.4.2** (partial) axe: document-title; HTML_CodeSniffer: 2_4_2.H25.1.NoTitleEl, 2_4_2.H25.1.EmptyTitle, 2_4_2.H25.2. Retest (7 failing cases): axe 5 flagged, 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 4 flagged, 3 missed. Rules catch missing or empty titles; whether the title describes topic or purpose is only a notice.
- **2.4.9** (partial) axe: link-name, identical-links-same-purpose; HTML_CodeSniffer: 2_4_9.H30. Retest (9 failing cases): axe 2 flagged, 2 asked for review, 5 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 flagged, 7 notice. Rules catch empty links; vague link text is a notice per link.
- **2.4.10** (none) axe: no rule; HTML_CodeSniffer: no sniff. Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. No rule decides whether content should be organised with headings.
- **2.5.3** (partial) axe: label-content-name-mismatch; HTML_CodeSniffer: no sniff. Retest (3 failing cases): axe 2 flagged, 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 flagged, 1 notice. axe's rule is experimental and covers some widgets; the retest detections came from missing-label rules on the same pages, not from a mismatch check.
- **3.1.1** (partial) axe: html-has-lang, html-lang-valid, html-xml-lang-mismatch; HTML_CodeSniffer: 3_1_1.H57.2, 3_1_1.H57.3.Lang. Retest (8 failing cases): axe 6 flagged, 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 4 flagged, 4 missed. Rules catch missing or invalid lang; a valid code for the wrong language passes.
- **3.1.2** (partial) axe: valid-lang; HTML_CodeSniffer: 3_1_2.H58.1.Lang, 3_1_2.H58. Retest (3 failing cases): axe 1 flagged, 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 3 missed. Rules catch invalid lang values on elements; passages in another language without lang are missed.
- **3.2.5** (partial) axe: meta-refresh-no-exceptions; HTML_CodeSniffer: 3_2_5.H83.3, 2_2_1.F40.2. Retest (3 failing cases): axe 2 flagged, 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 flagged, 2 missed; WCAG2AA supplement 3 flagged. Rules catch meta refresh and notice new-window links; script redirects and pop-ups are missed.
- **3.3.2** (partial) axe: label, form-field-multiple-labels; HTML_CodeSniffer: 1_3_1.F68, 3_3_2.G131,G89,G184,H90. Retest (3 failing cases): axe 3 flagged; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 flagged, 1 missed. Rules catch missing labels; whether labels and instructions suffice is a notice.
- **4.1.1** (partial) axe: duplicate-id, duplicate-id-active; HTML_CodeSniffer: 4_1_1.F77. Retest (5 failing cases): axe 4 flagged, 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 flagged, 4 missed. Removed in WCAG 2.2 (always satisfied for HTML). axe and HTML_CodeSniffer only check duplicate ids; an HTML validator (not in our toolset) could decide it fully. Some retest detections came from list rules.
- **4.1.2** (partial) axe: button-name, link-name, label, aria-required-attr, aria-valid-attr-value, aria-hidden-focus, frame-title, nested-interactive, select-name, input-button-name; HTML_CodeSniffer: 4_1_2.H91.A.NoContent, 4_1_2.H91.Button.Name, 4_1_2.H91.InputText.Name, 1_3_1.F68. Retest (16 failing cases): axe 11 flagged, 5 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 8 flagged, 8 missed. Rules catch missing names and invalid ARIA well; state and value updates on interaction are not tested.

## AI and human

Taken from the data file (`ai.level`, `human.level`). Levels: AI likely/possible/unlikely; human must/should/optional.

- **1.1.1** Non-text Content: AI likely (needs dom, accessibility-tree, screenshot); human should. AI: Comparing each image with its computed text alternative and surrounding text is a task vision models do well. Human: Equivalence for complex images (charts, diagrams) and context-dependent purpose needs confirmation.
- **1.3.1** Info and Relationships: AI likely (needs dom, accessibility-tree, screenshot); human should. AI: Comparing the visual structure in a screenshot with the semantics in the tree is a strength of current models. Human: Broad SC with many patterns; a person should confirm the AI's comparison.
- **1.3.5** Identify Input Purpose: AI likely (needs dom, accessibility-tree); human optional. AI: Matching field labels to the input-purpose list is a reliable reading task. Human: Markup inspection plus AI suffices.
- **1.3.6** Identify Purpose: AI possible (needs dom, accessibility-tree, screenshot); human should. AI: Landmarks are easy; deciding which icons and components need programmatic purpose is open-ended. Human: Scope of 'purpose' is interpretive.
- **2.4.1** Bypass Blocks: AI likely (needs dom, accessibility-tree, focus-trace); human optional. AI: Landmarks, headings and a working skip link are visible in tree and focus trace. Human: Tools plus AI suffice.
- **2.4.2** Page Titled: AI likely (needs dom, screenshot); human optional. AI: Judging a title against page content is an easy reading task. Human: Tools plus AI suffice.
- **2.4.9** Link Purpose (Link Only): AI likely (needs accessibility-tree); human optional. AI: Judging link names alone is a reading task. Human: AI suffices.
- **2.4.10** Section Headings: AI likely (needs dom, screenshot); human optional. AI: Spotting sections without headings is a structure-reading task. Human: AI suffices.
- **2.5.3** Label in Name: AI likely (needs screenshot, accessibility-tree); human optional. AI: Comparing visible label text with the accessible name is reliable. Human: AI suffices; speech-input testing confirms if wanted.
- **3.1.1** Language of Page: AI likely (needs dom); human optional. AI: Identifying the language of the text and comparing with lang is reliable. Human: Tools plus AI suffice.
- **3.1.2** Language of Parts: AI likely (needs dom); human optional. AI: Language identification of passages is reliable; proper names and loanwords are exceptions. Human: AI suffices.
- **3.2.5** Change on Request: AI likely (needs dom, interaction); human optional. AI: target attributes, redirects and pop-ups are detectable. Human: AI suffices.
- **3.3.2** Labels or Instructions: AI likely (needs dom, accessibility-tree, screenshot); human optional. AI: Reading labels and required-format hints is reliable. Human: Tools plus AI suffice.
- **4.1.1** Parsing: AI likely (needs dom); human optional. AI: Parsing errors are mechanical. Human: Tools suffice; consider adding a validator.
- **4.1.2** Name, Role, Value: AI likely (needs accessibility-tree, dom, interaction); human should. AI: Reading the tree before and after operating widgets checks names, roles, states and values. Human: Real assistive technology behaviour should be confirmed.

## Report

Write one finding per criterion and location. Use exactly these fields.

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| `criterion` | Success criterion id, for example `1.4.3` |
| `outcome` | `failed`, `passed`, `inapplicable` or `cantTell` |
| `location` | Page URL plus CSS selector of the element (or `page` for page-level findings) |
| `evidence` | One to three sentences of fact: what was observed, with numbers where they exist. Name the collected artifact (file name or step number in the trace) |
| `confidence` | `high`, `medium` or `low` |
| `tester` | `human` or the model id of the AI that judged |

Rules:
- `failed` needs evidence that shows the failure; do not write it from a guess.
- `passed` means that this tester checked the criterion across the collected data and found no failure; it is not a conformance claim.
- `inapplicable` means the content the criterion is about does not exist on the page (state which content you looked for).
- `cantTell` means the data cannot decide it. Say what is missing and which pass or person could decide.
- One finding per element and criterion; do not merge different locations.

Example (JSON, one finding):

```json
{"criterion": "2.4.7", "outcome": "failed", "location": "https://example.org/form#nav a.skip", "evidence": "No visible change between focused and blurred crops at focus step 3 (focus-trace/step-03.png): outline is none, no replacement style.", "confidence": "medium", "tester": "claude-sonnet-5-5"}
```

## Sources

- WCAG 2.2, W3C Recommendation, <https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/>, and its Understanding documents, <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/>, linked per criterion above.
- Techniques and failures, <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/> (failure ids Fxx are listed per criterion from `data/wcag/success-criteria.json`).
- W3C, *ACT Rules Format 1.1*, <https://www.w3.org/TR/act-rules-format-1.1/> (outcomes passed, failed, inapplicable, cantTell); see [ACT Rules](../../wiki/sources/act-rules.md). ACT rule ids are not cited here because they were not verified; look up rules at <https://act-rules.github.io/rules/>.
- [Triage data](../../data/mappings/sc-test-methods.json) and [decision D-025](../../wiki/decisions.md).
- Chrome DevTools Protocol, Accessibility domain, <https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/tot/Accessibility/>; Nu HTML Checker, <https://validator.github.io/validator/>.
- Nav, test protocol *Kodesjekk og skjermlesertest*, <https://aksel.nav.no/god-praksis/artikler/testprotokoll-kodesjekk-og-skjermlesertest> (see [Nav guidance](../../wiki/sources/nav-testing-guidance.md)).
